subject: [PATCH 0/6] nfsd: add new export options for controlling read/write iomode

reviews.author: Chuck Lever
reviews.summary: The reviewer noted that nfsd_io_cache_read_set() still sets nfsd_disable_splice_read based on the global knob, which prevents splice from being used even when a per-export setting is made for riomode=buffered. This creates an inconsistency between the global and per-export settings.
reviews.raw_body:
nfsd_io_cache_read_set() still sets nfsd_disable_splice_read whenever
the global knob is switched to dontcache or direct, so
nfsd_read_splice_ok() returns false before this per-export test is
reached. An export pinned to riomode=buffered on such a server never
gets splice; it falls through to nfsd_iter_read() and does vector
buffered reads. The same applies to the splice_ok decisions in
nfsd4_encode_read() and nfsd4_encode_read_plus_data().

Patch 3/6 says an explicit per-export setting pins that export's
IO mode "regardless of the global knob", and that isn't quite true
now for the buffered case.

I need to think carefully about the interaction between the "disable
splice" setting, which is global, and the per-export I/O setting.

Separately, on the names of the export options: "riomode" and
"wiomode" are hard to read, and "mode" might suggest "permission bits"
to an administrator. How about read_io= and write_io= instead? They
follow the underscore style of the other multi-word export options
(no_subtree_check, root_squash, security_label) and read naturally:

  /srv/data  client(rw,read_io=direct,write_io=dontcache)

The values buffered, dontcache, and direct then carry the meaning
without "cache" or "mode" in the name.

The name appears in the exports syntax, the nfsd.export/content
output, the netlink YAML spec, and the forthcoming nfs-utils series,
so it's worth settling before v2 and before the nfs-utils side gets
merged.


-- 
Chuck Lever (Come to NFS bake-a-thon! https://nfsv4bat.org)

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: Author suggests making the 'disable_splice' feature a separate export option, implying it's not yet part of the patch series
reviews.raw_body:
Maybe disable_splice should be an export option of its own? It seems
like that should be doable.

reviews.author: Chuck Lever
reviews.summary: Reviewer Chuck Lever questioned whether adding new export options for controlling read/write iomode should be a permanent extension of the export options API, suggesting it might not be desirable.
reviews.raw_body:
That would be easy to implement, but I wonder if it's something we want
to carry as a permanent extension of the export options API.


-- 
Chuck Lever (Come to NFS bake-a-thon! https://nfsv4bat.org)

2026-10-27.patch_summary: This patch series adds new export options to the NFS daemon (nfsd) that allow administrators to control the read and write I/O modes on a per-export basis. The options, riomode= and wiomode=, can be set to buffered, direct, or dontcache, and override global debugfs switches. This change is intended to make it easier for users to fine-tune their NFS performance by allowing them to set I/O modes on a per-export basis. The patch also includes new documentation to help administrators choose the right I/O mode settings. A companion patchset in nfs-utils will add support for these options and provide tools to help users configure them.
